
Various exponential distributions are shown in the visualisation below, for different values of $\lambda = 1/\beta$.




```{r, ExpDemo, echo=FALSE, fig.align="center", fig.cap="Exponential distributions."}
lambdas <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10)

### Build x grid and densities for each lambda  ###
traces <- lapply(lambdas, function(lambda) {
  x    <- seq(0, 
              10, 
              length.out = 600)
  y  <- dexp(x, 
             rate = lambda)
  list(x = x, 
       y = y, 
       lambda = lambda)
})

### Build figure  ###
fig <- plot_ly(width = 600, 
               height = 400)

for (i in seq_along(lambdas)) {
  vis <- (i == 3)   # default
  fig <- fig %>%
    add_lines(x = traces[[i]]$x, 
              y = traces[[i]]$y,
              visible    = vis,
              name = paste0("Lambda =", lambdas[i]),
              showlegend = FALSE,
              line       = list(color = "steelblue", width = 2.5))
}

###  One button per lambda  ###
lambda_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(lambdas), function(i) {
  vis <- rep(FALSE, length(lambdas) * 2)
  vis[i] <- TRUE
  list(
    method = "update",
    args   = list(
      list(visible = as.list(vis)),
      list(title  = paste0("Lambda = ", lambdas[i]))
    ),
    label  = paste0("lambda = ", lambdas[i])
  )
})

fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title  = list(text = "PDF of an exponential distribution",
                x = 0.5,
                xanchor = "center"),
  xaxis  = list(title = "X"),
  yaxis  = list(title = "Density"),
   margin = list(t = 60, 
                 b = 110),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", 
                x = 0.65, 
                y = 1.0),
  updatemenus = list(
    list(
      type      = "buttons",
      direction = "right",
      x         = 0.0,
      y         = -0.28,
      xanchor   = "left",
      buttons   = lambda_buttons
    )
  )
) %>%
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE)

fig
```
